clue.text: Criticise judge and peculiar potentate

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
rum is an old British word for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a judge and some odd ruler at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandly self-important official or ruler is mockingly called by this name, so it suits a potentate.

clue.text: Have the last word here

parts.note: read as the word said at the very end of a prayer or hymn, which congregations speak together

explanation.definitionFit: This Hebrew word meaning 'so be it' closes prayers, so it is literally the final word spoken.

clue.text: Legal expert quite without religious instruction

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: just can mean quite, as in 'just right'
RI is the British school abbreviation for religious instruction

explanation.surface: A lawyer is said to be utterly lacking in any religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense of outside, so it works as a container signal. Religious instruction was a subject taught in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A jurist is a scholar of law, an authority on legal matters.

clue.text: I repeatedly snore, sadly creating more din

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters are in a sorry state and must be rearranged
repeatedly says the letter I is used twice over in the wordplay

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that their snoring keeps getting louder, to everyone's misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I repeatedly' gives II; add SNORE and rearrange all seven letters, as 'sadly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Making more din means being louder, a comparative of noisy.

clue.text: Regrets some untrue statements

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry for a few lies they have told.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it, so both words name feeling sorry.

clue.text: I'd see MD involved in wrongful act

indicators.note: involved suggests letters tangled together, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters are I, D, S, E, E, M and D

explanation.surface: Someone expects to see a doctor implicated in some malpractice.
explanation.walkthrough: MD (Doctor of Medicine) looks like a person in the scene, but it simply supplies two letters to the anagram signalled by 'involved'.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeed is a wrongdoing or offence, an act that breaks the rules.

clue.text: It's just one thing after the other!

definitions.text: It's just one thing after the other!

parts.words: It's just one thing after the other!
parts.note: the weary complaint is read literally, as a line of people or vehicles moving forward one behind another

explanation.definitionFit: A parade moves in an orderly line, each participant following the one before.

clue.text: Man who is noble yet heartless has to be seen in Exeter maybe

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word yet is taken away

parts.note: to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A nobleman with no heart has to make an appearance in a Devon city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle E from YET, leaving YT. Exeter is the county town of Devon, the administrative centre of an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is one example of a town that serves as the seat of government for its county.

clue.text: Liveliness one's found in religious brother

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Bro is a short form of brother, a title given to a monk or friar
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Some vitality is discovered in a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or verve, a spirited liveliness of manner.

clue.text: Rise and hasten out, demonstrating joviality

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Get up and rush out of the house with a cheerful air.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RISE and HASTEN are rearranged, as 'out' signals; 'demonstrating' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartiness is warm, cheerful exuberance, much like jollity.

clue.text: Some deride a Conservative minister

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people mock a Tory government minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is a clergyman in some churches, ranking below a priest, who ministers to the congregation.

clue.text: Place near Liverpool good for getting illegal stuff

parts.note: Bootle is a town on Merseyside, just north of Liverpool

explanation.surface: A town near Liverpool is a good spot to pick up contraband.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTLE is a town beside Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg describes goods, especially alcohol or recordings, made or sold unlawfully.

clue.text: Musical groups making money with g & s, but getting a note wrong

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: a musical note letter is swapped for another, so G becomes B

parts.note: the ampersand is read as the word and, giving G AND S

explanation.surface: Musicians earn cash playing Gilbert and Sullivan, though one of them hits a bum note.
explanation.walkthrough: G & S suggests Gilbert and Sullivan, but read it as G AND S; 'getting a note wrong' replaces the note G with the note B, giving BANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensembles of trumpets, cornets and tubas are groups of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Individual going round Lesotho, wild, escaping from prison

indicators.note: going round says the first piece encircles the second

parts.note: one can mean a single individual

indicators.note: wild signals that the letters run riot and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone figure roams wildly around the African kingdom of Lesotho after a jailbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges the kingdom's name into THELOOS, and 'going round' wraps the word for an individual around it, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict who has broken out is free and at large.

clue.text: Continue chattering in the country

parts.note: gab is idle chattering, as in 'the gift of the gab'
on means continuing, as in 'carry on'

explanation.surface: People keep on talking while in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'gab on' means to keep chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a nation on the west coast of Africa.

clue.text: Socialite, pernickety, female out to get composer

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society

indicators.note: out says the following letter is removed from the word

parts.note: fussy means pernickety, overly particular

explanation.surface: A fussy society girl is ousted so that a composer can be brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' removes F (female) from FUSSY, leaving USSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was a French composer, famous for Clair de Lune.

clue.text: One of two in 23 maybe!

parts.note: the number 23 looks like a cross-reference, but it is just a number written with a 2 and a 3

explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords use numbers like 23 to point to other clues, so a solver goes looking for clue 23; here it is just the number itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral such as 2 or 3 is a single figure, one of the characters making up a number.

clue.text: Fanatical artist offered amount

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a bid is the amount offered at an auction

explanation.surface: An obsessive painter puts in an offer at the auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means extreme or zealous in one's views, like a fervent fanatic.

clue.text: A distant world — no place for car

indicators.note: no says the letters for place are dropped from the word

parts.note: Pluto is a far-off world at the edge of the solar system
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A remote planet offers no room for a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No place' removes PL from PLUTO, leaving UTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is a short form of automobile, a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Writer of 9, twisted inside

indicators.note: twisted inside says the letters within the word are turned around while its ends stay put

parts.note: the answer to 9 across, a word for liveliness

explanation.surface: A pen made from 9 across, its innards warped.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle letters R and I swap places in BRIO, the answer to 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A biro is a ballpoint pen, an instrument used for writing.

clue.text: Theme of a thousand old books and one poem

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
OT is the Old Testament, the older books of the Bible
If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: The subject is a thousand antique volumes plus a single poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If—' is Kipling's poem of advice to his son, famous in Britain and a common crossword source.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea or design element running through a work.

clue.text: Hurt short English writer

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
being low on something means being short of it

explanation.surface: An Englishman of small stature takes a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan playwright, author of Doctor Faustus.

clue.text: Enthusiast observes, it's said, and desires

indicators.note: it's said signals that the words are spoken, so they sound like another word

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast and sees means observes

explanation.surface: A keen supporter watches, and wants things, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancies, as a noun, are whims or longings, just like wishes or yearnings.

clue.text: Book presented by marines to an American commander

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A volume is handed over by marines to a US officer.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE is a famous Victorian adventure novel. William Tecumseh Sherman was a Union general in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: General Sherman led Union armies in the US Civil War, so he was a military leader.

clue.text: Given accommodation, yet deceived

definitions.meaning: a lodger or refugee is housed when offered a room
being fooled by a con or trick

explanation.surface: A guest is given a room but has been conned.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both lodging someone in your home and being fooled by a swindle.

clue.text: English girl failing to finish cake

indicators.note: the girl's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Claire is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An English girl doesn't complete her pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to finish' drops the last E from CLAIRE, leaving CLAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a cream-filled choux pastry, a small cake.

clue.text: Report of a letter giving declaration

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are spoken and sound like another word

parts.note: a vowel is a letter, such as A or E

explanation.surface: Reading a letter aloud gives a public statement.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open statement or admission, like a solemn declaration.

clue.text: Place that sounds like a small room

indicators.note: these words tell the solver to listen for a word with the same sound

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet, a small room

explanation.surface: A location whose name sounds like the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British for a toilet; the French word for place (as in 'in lieu of') sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu is French for place, used in English in phrases such as 'in lieu of', meaning instead of.

clue.text: Seaweed deposited in coastal gale

indicators.note: deposited in says the answer is lodged inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Seaweed is washed up during a coastal storm.
explanation.definitionFit: An alga is a simple water plant, and seaweeds are large marine examples.

clue.text: One drink taken in by mouth to start with

indicators.note: taken in says the first pieces are placed inside the word for by mouth

parts.note: medicine taken by mouth is taken orally
one is the Roman numeral I
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A single drink swallowed by mouth at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' puts the numeral and the spirit inside the word for by mouth, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at the outset, initially or in the beginning, was done in the first place.

clue.text: Striking run

definitions.meaning: ... as a noun is flair or striking style, as in 'cut a ...'
a short fast run, a sprint

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stylish panache, which makes a striking show, and a sudden quick sprint.

clue.text: Rider in pursuit, a rein loosely hanging around

indicators.note: hanging around says the shuffled letters surround the other piece
loosely suggests the letters are slackened and rearranged

parts.note: a quest is a pursuit or search

explanation.surface: A horseman in a chase with his rein dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loosely' rearranges A REIN into ERIAN, and 'hanging around' wraps it around QUEST, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian is a horse rider.
